title: Crime Classics
paragraphs: CBS historical true-crime docudrama created, produced and directed by Elliott Lewis. Lou Merrill’s Thomas Hyland frames independently dramatized crimes drawn from historical records, court reports and newspapers.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS summer replacement run (June 15, 1953 to September 7, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and CBS regular-season run (September 30, 1953 to June 30, 1954) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Bernard Herrmann (composer, conductor, and arranger), David Friedkin (writer), Elliott Lewis (director, producer, and performer), Lou Merrill (host and performer), Morton Fine (writer), Bob Lemond (announcer), and Ben Wright (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to family, marriage and domestic murder, murder and homicide, execution, hanging and capital punishment, trial, evidence and historical justice, conspiracy, accomplices and group crime, and assassination and political killing.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Primary-record historical crime reconstruction, CBS sustaining true-crime anthology, Military-network rebroadcast circulation, and Historically suggestive minimalist radio scoring.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
